{{Quote|You spent seven seasons with the Circus Horrificus, training their specimens without being eaten. That's a record for them, you know.|[[Bib Fortuna/Legends|Bib Fortuna]]|<ref name="RKT">{{StoryCite|story=A Boy and His Monster: The Rancor Keeper's Tale|book=Tales from Jabba's Palace}}</ref>}}
'''Malakili''' was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Human/Legends|Human]] from the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core World]] of [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]], a creature tamer and servant of the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] gangster [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]] on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. Malakili took care of [[Jabba's rancor/Legends|Jabba's rancor]].

==Biography==
===Early life===
A [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]], Malakili was [[Reproduction/Legends|born]] on [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]],<ref name="CharEnc" /> a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] best known for its [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]], its fast [[Starship/Legends|starships]], and skilled merchants.<ref name="AGTSWU2">''[[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe, Second Edition, Revised and Expanded]]''</ref> Since his most tender [[Youngling/Legends|childhood]], the young Malakili was fascinated by wild animals, and he wished he could dedicate his life to taking care of them.<ref name="FF114">{{FactFile|114|RAN 3-4|Rancor Keeper}}</ref> By [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], the [[Corellian/Legends|Corellian]] became involved with [[Gargonn]] the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt's]] [[Circus Horrificus/Legends|Circus Horrificus]],<ref name="EtM5">[[Star Wars (1998) 17|''Star Wars'' (1998) 17]]</ref> a traveling menagerie that displayed monstrous creatures throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], for which he became a professional beast handler and monster trainer. Quickly, it became obvious that Malakili's touch was inimitable. Only he knew how to tend the circus' restless beasts while avoiding undue risk. Aside from the bloodthirsty creatures themselves, Malakili became the true star of the Circus Horrificus.<ref name="RKT" />

===Incident on Nar Shaddaa===
{{Quote|An illegal performance by the underground Circus Horrificus ended in chaos yesterday in the lower levels of Nar Shaddaa as a new, exotic beast showcased by the traveling troupe escaped and ran amuck.|Extract from a HoloNet News report|<ref name="HNN52">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|52|regional/13418_3.html|Circus Horrificus Turns Horrific}}</ref>}}
Despite the Corellian's unequalled skills, accidents remained possible. In the fourth [[Standard month/Legends|month]] of [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], an unexpected event took place while the menagerie was performing in the [[Ko Hentota]] district of [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]]. One of the wrangler's beasts, an aggressive [[arqet]], got rid of its restraints and attacked the spectators, killing twelve in the process. The Corellian attempted to stun the arqet, but to no avail. While the murderous creature crawled into the district's ventilation grid, Malakili and the other surviving members of the Circus vacated the premises.<ref name="HNN52" />

===Slave of the Hutt===
{{Quote|I think this is a rancor. I have heard of them, but never dreamed that I would be lucky enough to see one in my lifetime.|Malakili to Bib Fortuna|<ref name="RKT" />}}
[[File:Malakili-humiliated.png|thumb|left|200px|Like many of the Hutt's employees, Malakili had to suffer humiliations from Jabba.]]
Following that incident, the Circus Horrificus sold Malakili to [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]],<ref name="RKT" /> a Hutt [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] and shipping magnate in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="HNN48">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|48|regional/13321_5.html|Zorba the Hutt Sentenced to 45 Years}}</ref> Although his contract file mentioned that he was "transferred," the Corellian knew that he had been purchased like a [[Slavery/Legends|slave]] and would be left at the mercy of Jabba, probably for the rest of his life. Nonetheless, the wrangler was mild-mannered and friendly with many of Jabba's crowd, such as [[Porcellus/Legends|Porcellus]] and [[J'Quille/Legends|J'Quille]]. He viewed the rancor as a kindhearted creature and a friend. At one point, the bloodthirsty gamblers demanded more violence. So Jabba ordered Malakili to train the rancor for battle, and had a special weapon harness built.<ref name="RKT" /> Malakili fitted the rancor with the weapons harness and entered his master's dangerous [[Jabba's demolition games|demolition derby]].<ref name="SWD">''[[Star Wars: Demolition]]''</ref> Malakili and his mount, however, did not emerge victorious in the contest. As a cruel punishment, the wrangler was forced to endure humiliation by [[Salacious B. Crumb/Legends|Salacious B. Crumb]], Jabba's court jester, who sat on his shoulders dancing and giggling madly in front of the whole court.<ref name="Canon SWD">In the video game ''[[Star Wars: Demolition]]'', Malakili's winning cutscene had the [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] dancer [[Lyn Me/Legends|Lyn Me]] eaten by [[Jabba's rancor/Legends|Jabba's rancor]]. However, the ''[[Star Wars Trilogy Sourcebook, Special Edition]]'' established that Lyn Me survived Jabba the Hutt, which renders the wrangler's winning cutscene non-[[canon]]. In the losing cutscene, Malakili was humiliated by Jabba and [[Salacious B. Crumb/Legends|Salacious B. Crumb]] for being defeated.</ref> Nevertheless, Malakili forged a close bond with the rancor, such that the creature would allow him to treat its wounds and eat meals with it.<ref name="RKT" />

In [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]],<ref name="SWG_timeline">{{SWG_timeline}}</ref> Malakili recruited a spacer to help him to achieve several tasks. He first tasked the spacer to kill several [[Jundland Wastes/Legends|Jundland]] [[Eopie/Legends|eopies]] and collect their livers in order to feed the [[Sarlacc/Legends|sarlacc]] of the [[Great Pit of Carkoon/Legends|Great Pit of Carkoon]]. Malakili then tasked the spacer to get a sample of DNA from the [[Western Dune Sea/Legends|Western Dune Sea]] [[Krayt dragon/Legends|krayt dragon]] skeleton. The skeleton was supposed to belong to an ancient krayt dragon more powerful than any other dragon and Jabba wanted to use the DNA in experiments. Malakili next tasked the spacer to explore and search [[Ben Kenobi's home/Legends|Ben Kenobi's hut]]. The spacer found a fossilized resonance chamber from a krayt dragon that [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] used to terrify [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Tusken Raiders]]. In recognition for this work, Malakili finally accepted to give to Jabba's [[Supervisor droid/Legends|supervisor droid]] [[EV-9D9/Legends|EV-9D9]] the [[Shock rod/Legends|shock rods]] she needed to maintain discipline among her droids.<ref name="SWG:SR">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=class|Legacy|Shock Rods|Tatooine}}</ref>

At some point during his time on Tatooine, Malakili killed a giant mutated [[Womp rat/Legends|womp rat]] that had taken over a cave owned by [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Tusken Raiders]], and got a [[Gaderffii/Legends|gaderffii]] stick as a gift from them.

He was planning on betraying Jabba to [[Lady/Legends|Lady]] [[Valarian/Legends|Valarian]] and leaving with the rancor because Jabba planned on pitting it against a [[Krayt dragon/Legends|Krayt dragon]], which would surely kill it. He even hid a camera for her in Jabba's throne room. When [[Gonar]] threatened to blackmail Malakili with evidence of the planned betrayal, Malakili murdered him and fed the body to the rancor.

When [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] killed the rancor, Malakili wept painfully. His assistant [[Giran/Legends|Giran]], despite not being fond of the rancor, attempted to comfort him. After Jabba's death at the [[Great Pit of Carkoon/Legends|Great Pit of Carkoon]], Malakili broke the cook, [[Porcellus/Legends|Porcellus]], out of Jabba's dungeon, and they went on to found a restaurant in [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]] called the [[Crystal Moon Restaurant/Legends|Crystal Moon]] Restaurant.<ref name="Epilogue: Whatever Became Of...?">{{StoryCite|story=Epilogue: Whatever Became Of...?|book=Tales from Jabba's Palace}}</ref><ref name="CharEnc" />

==Personality and traits==
[[File:Malakili-Circus-Horrificus.jpg|thumb|200px|Malakili employed by Circus Horrificus in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]]]]
A large Human, Malakili was muscular from wrestling monsters and lifting heavy objects. However, his star status at the Circus Horrificus came with its feasts of plentiful food, and Malakili's belly had grown large and fat. The wrangler, however, did not care much for his physical appearance. He was not interested in impressing any sentient being and only wanted his monsters to hold him in respect. He usually wore a simple [[loincloth]] and a draped black headdress.<ref name="RKT" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|I like the idea that everyone loves someone. And even the worst, most horrible monster you can imagine was loved by his keeper. And the rancor probably loved his keeper.|[[George Lucas]]|<ref name="Making of ROTJ">''[[The Making of Return of the Jedi]]''</ref>}}
Malakili first appeared in [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']], the third installment of the [[original trilogy]]. He was portrayed by an uncredited [[Paul Brooke]], but his sobs were provided by [[Ernie Fosselius]].

In [[2000]], [[Jess Harnell]] voiced Malakili in the video game ''[[Star Wars: Demolition]]''. That game had two possible endings for Malakili: he either won or lost Jabba's demolition derby. The "losing cutscene" showed Jabba and Salacious B. Crumb humiliating the wrangler. If he won, a cutscene showed the rancor eating [[Lyn Me/Legends|Lyn Me]] as a reward. However, Lyn Me was still alive during the events of ''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'', which occurred shortly after those of ''Demolition.'' This indicates that Malakili did not win the demolition games, making his "losing cutscene" official.

The [[Ewok Handler]]'s model in ''[[Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption]]'' is actually that of Malakili, but the game makes no mention of him.
